headline: Southborough secured a $3.9 million culvert grant to avoid new debt, while school projects advanced and town meeting dates were scheduled.
synopsis: In June, Southborough secured nearly $3.9 million in state culvert grant funding, eliminating the need to issue municipal debt previously approved by Town Meeting. The Neary Elementary School roof replacement advanced into construction after bids came in at $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million appropriation, while a $165,000 feasibility study got underway to explore elementary facility options. In a 3-2 vote, the Select Board approved spending $105,000 in unspent police department salaries to purchase an Axon drone system, offset by a private school gift. The Wastewater Study Committee voted down a $30,000 consultant study, postponing a Route 9 sewer financing article from the fall warrant. Additionally, the Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027.

top_items.title: $3.9 million state culvert grant avoids municipal debt
top_items.why: Southborough received nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program. The award fully replaces previously authorized borrowing for culvert replacements.
top_items.body: The Select Board announced that Southborough was awarded nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program. Because Town Meeting had previously approved $3.9 million in borrowing for culvert infrastructure replacements, the state grant will allow the town to complete the projects without issuing new debt.

top_items.title: Neary School roof bids arrive under budget at $2.8 million
top_items.why: Bids for the Neary Elementary School roof replacement totaled roughly $2.8 million, well below the $4.5 million Town Meeting appropriation. Construction starts in late June.
top_items.body: The School Committee reviewed bid results for the Neary Elementary School roof replacement project. Combined low bids came in at approximately $2.8 million, well under the $4.5 million appropriation approved at Town Meeting. Construction is slated to start in late June, prompting the summer Southborough Extended Day Program to relocate to Finn Elementary School.

top_items.title: Select Board approves $105,000 police drone package
top_items.why: In a 3-2 vote, the Select Board authorized purchasing an Axon drone system using unspent year-end police salary funds. The purchase includes a $20,000 gift from Fay School.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted 3-2 to authorize Police Chief Ryan Newell to use surplus year-end department funds to purchase a $105,000 five-year drone package from Axon, offset by a $20,000 contribution from Fay School. While the Capital Improvement Planning Committee recommended the drone program as a safety priority, board members debated the financial policy of funding a major capital acquisition through operational budget surplus rather than a Town Meeting vote.

top_items.title: Neary School feasibility contract executed with Tappé Architects
top_items.why: The Select Board approved a $165,000 contract with Tappé Architects for elementary school facility planning. The committee kicked off work to examine options for Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted 5-0 to approve a $165,000 contract with Tappé Architects to lead the feasibility study and schematic design for the Neary Elementary School building project. The Elementary School Building Committee subsequently held a kickoff session with the firm, directing the architects to develop multiple flexible options without eliminating voter-approved alternatives ahead of future Town Meetings.

top_items.title: Wastewater Committee rejects $30,000 Route 9 financial study
top_items.why: The Wastewater Study Committee voted unanimously against spending $30,000 on an economic consulting study for Route 9 sewer financing. The decision postpones a planned Fall Town Meeting article.
top_items.body: The Wastewater Study Committee voted 0-5 against spending $30,000 to hire Camoin Associates for an economic development and District Improvement Financing (DIF) study. Although the Select Board had previously authorized reallocating the funds from the Economic Development Committee budget, committee members concluded that spending the money was premature until physical site feasibility and watershed restrictions are confirmed, effectively deferring a DIF warrant article for Fall Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Town Meeting dates set for October 2026 and March 2027
top_items.why: The Select Board scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted unanimously to schedule the Fall Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM. The board also established the date for the 2027 Annual Town Meeting, setting it for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10:00 AM.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 scaled back to footbridge application
top_items.why: After total project estimates exceeded $600,000, the Trails Committee removed a planned boardwalk to seek CPA funds solely for a reservoir footbridge.
top_items.body: Facing construction bids that exceeded available funding, the Trails Committee voted to adjust its Phase 2 Community Preservation Act request by removing a planned wetland boardwalk and rerouting that section onto a natural surface trail. The committee finalized an application estimated at $440,000 to $450,000 focusing exclusively on the reservoir footbridge and abutments, which received unanimous support letters from both the Conservation Commission and Recreation Commission.
